provenance.generated_from: Issue #120 Phase 4.4: deterministic rules fingerprinting two real, documented upstream regressions. Rule 1 cites upstream issue #629 (installer flips ccache in /etc/makepkg.conf permanently; closed 2026-09-06) - verified against the upstream issue body. Rule 2 fingerprints the dual-updater state-desync symptom; the mission brief called it '#818', but upstream issue #818 is unrelated ('CAELESTIA-KDE OVERHAUL', a PR-template issue) - the actual, verified issue is #565 ('Two independent update mechanisms share version-tracking state but pull from different repo checkouts', still OPEN), so the rule cites #565 and the discrepancy is recorded in the CHANGELOG.

rules.title: Update state desync: Nexus pending-commit count does not match your clone / uncommitted changes lost after 'Install Updates' (dual-updater symptom, PRE-fix versions)

fix.text: Upstream issue #565 (OPEN): two updaters write the same version-tracking files from different checkouts. `update.sh` deploys from your real clone; the Nexus 'Install Updates' button (caelestia-update) deploys from a private shadow clone at ~/.config/caelestia-update/repo. Alternating between them desyncs the pending-commit badge and can overwrite uncommitted work.
Check which commit the shell thinks it is running vs. your real clone:

Pick ONE updater path and stick to it: dev-workflow users should use update.sh from their clone and avoid the Nexus button (or vice versa); the two must not alternate until upstream fixes the shared state.
Before any future update: commit or stash local edits in your real clone first - the shadow-clone path does not stash them for you.

undo.text: If uncommitted edits were overwritten, check `git -C ~/caelestia-dots-kde reflog` and `git stash list` - but note the shadow clone never touched the real clone's git state, so recovery depends on your own history.

rules.clarify_probe: Paste the output of: cat ~/.config/quickshell/caelestia/.current_commit && git -C ~/caelestia-dots-kde rev-parse HEAD - and confirm which updater ran last (update.sh from your clone, or the Nexus 'Install Updates' button).
